newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-AUSTRIANS TO DEMAND DAVIS CUP MONEY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRIANS TO DEMAND DAVIS CUP MONEY.

text.p: The Austrian Tennis Federation (OTV) said on Friday it would appeal against the ITF's verdict that it must forfeit $59,000 in prize money for failing to complete last month's Davis Cup tie against Brazil.

At a meeting in London on Monday, the International Tennis Federation also confirmed the result which gave Brazil a 4-1 victory over Austria. Attempts by the OTV to have the tie replayed on neutral ground failed.
"We will not protest the result because that would be unrealistic. But we do want the advertising part of the prize money," OTV vice-president Christian Ransmayer told the Austrian newsagency APA.
Ransmayer said the OTV would demand the sum earned through advertising, some $40,000 of the $59,000.
The Austrian Davis Cup team refused to complete the tie in Sao Paolo after world number three Thomas Muster walked out of the doubles, saying he felt threatened by the crowd.
Ransmayer said the OTV fully backed and respected Muster's decision to abandon the tie and expected the ITF to next address the matter in December.
